description:
**Divergence**
Upstream (pi-mono interactive-mode.ts L3549-3568, restoreQueuedMessagesToEditor):
- Drain ALL queued messages.
- Join with \"\\n\\n\".
- Set editor text to (queued || \"\") joined with current editor text.
- Optionally call agent.abort() (used by Escape during streaming).
- This *is* the only way to edit queued message text upstream.

Octo_pi (interactive.ex L1218-1226 + handle_dequeue_key/3 L1765-1793):
- Drain → show in a dedicated overlay.
- Arrow keys to navigate, Backspace/Delete to remove items, Escape to
  re-enqueue what's left.
- No way to edit the *content* of any queued message.

**Why this matters**
1. Upstream parity: documented keybinding \"app.message.dequeue\" / \"alt+up\"
   has the description \"Edit queued messages\", not \"View / delete queued
   messages\".
2. Editing text — the most common reason a user wants to revisit a queued
   message is to refine it, not just remove it wholesale.
3. The overlay's re-enqueue-on-Escape preserves order only if drain
   returns FIFO and re-enqueue is FIFO; coupled with bug opi-tze.4 the
   re-enqueue path is broken.

**Fix sketch**
Replace the dequeue overlay with the upstream model:
- On Alt+Up: drain all queued items, join with blank-line separators,
  prepend to current editor text, refocus the input.
- Drop the dequeue_overlay state and overlay rendering.
- Pair with Escape-while-streaming: drain queue back to editor AND abort
  (matches upstream restoreQueuedMessagesToEditor({abort: true})).
title: [FEATURE] Dequeue UX: restore queued messages back into editor (upstream parity)
